page: The UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor configured with 4 vCPUs and 4 physical cores running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, meaning resources are distributed among multiple tenants. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of strong single-core performance and average multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2758.58, and single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 33.57 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 9375.63 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5462.0. Memory performance shows a significant bottleneck for large datasets, with uncached large-block read bandwidth falling into the bottom 10% at 6.32 GB/sec, while small-block cached read bandwidth remains average at 563.42 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and starter-tier hardware profile, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The weak performance in Passmark memory testing and Redis SET operations highlights limitations for memory-intensive or high-throughput database applications. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, light software compilation, and basic text or image processing.
